thread:
ashley-ops: Customer reported p99 spikes ~2pm UTC in eu-west. They say tail latency for embed endpoint jumped from 120ms to 900ms intermittently. Logged ticket 12345. attaching quick graphs.

oncall-bot: Alert: eu-west/embed-p99 > 800ms for 15m. Pager duty trig: infra-embed-p99.

priya-sre: Thanks. Any rollout around that window? kernel/driver/firmware? :thinking: 

ashley-ops: We pushed driver 535.12 to eu-west at 1:40 UTC and a kernel security patch at 1:55 UTC. Both rolled via canary groups then expanded.

sam-eng: Ok that's suspicious. Do we have io wait / nvme queue depth spikes? Can you paste top-level iostat / ioping trends?

danielle-ml: Customer trace shows long host read times while fetching KV cache shards. Sample from their trace:

```
2025-03-10T13:59:42Z GET /embed -> backend read 0.89s (nvme qdepth 64 -> 8)
2025-03-10T14:01:03Z GET /embed -> backend read 0.72s (nvme qdepth 64 -> 8)
```

priya-sre: That's consistent with host qdepth throttle after driver change. We saw similar signals in canary but thought transient.

evan-eng: I just checked host metrics: per-host nvme_io_pending jumped, scheduler wait increased, and GPU utilization dropped. Looks like storage bottleneck causing scheduling backlog -> tokenization queues bloated.

sam-eng: Two mitigations: 1) Roll back driver on the affected pool to previous 530.x, 2) Temporarily divert embed traffic to a different hw pool with older firmware.

ashley-ops: Rolling rollback on 6 nodes in eu-west now (group: embed-pool-b) using our infra playbook. `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` then reprovision older driver image.

oncall-bot: Runbook step executed: rollback job started by ashley-ops at 14:12 UTC. Notifying customers: support will follow up in 30m.

priya-sre: Also add kernel param tweak to reduce hostfs writeback pressure as a short-term: sysctl vm.dirty_background_ratio=5 (we'll test on canary first)

danielle-ml: Observed immediate improvement on first rolled back host: embed p99 dropped to 140ms within 2 min. Customer confirms partial relief.

ashley-ops: Good. Will continue rollback across remaining nodes. Opening incident postmortem ticket and tagging eng-runtime, eng-infra, and support.

sam-eng: Postmortem action items: more conservative rollout gating for driver+kernel combos, automated nvme qdepth baseline checks, and add a canary workload that stresses KV read tail latency.

evan-eng: I'll start a bisect job to isolate which driver commit introduces qdepth throttling. Also we should add obs: expose nvme qdepth and queue latency in per-model dashboards.

ashley-ops: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup: Customer update drafted and sent.
